scope: Corollary 7.1 (Nontrivial smooth A3-fibrations) of the manuscript “An explicit failure of complex affine-space cancellation” (preprints/An-explicit-failure-of-complex-affine-space-cancellation-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 047 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 91a1a2f28c960cba), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let P, H, A be as in (1.2), and put X = Spec A. Write A1 p = Spec C[p] and A2 p,q = Spec C[p, q], where q is independent of p. Consider the morphisms π : X −→ A1 p, ρ = (p, H) : Spec P = A5 −→ A2 p,q, induced respectively by C[p] → A and by C[p, q] → P with q 7→ H. Both are smooth surjective morphisms of relative dimension three. For either morphism and every point y of its base, the fiber over y is isomorphic to A3 κ(y); in particular, every geometric fiber is affine three-space. Neither morphism is a Zariski-locally trivial A3-bundle. Thus the Dolgachev–Weisfeiler affine- fibration conjecture fails in relative dimension three over each of the smooth complex affine bases A1 and A2.
